The poll, released on Sunday, Sept. 6, found that only 32% of Americans approved of Trump’s job performance, a three-point drop from last month’s edition and the lowest the president has seen in Focaldata/Financial Times tracking since it began in May.

AP News' poll from the Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research says Trump's approval rating stands at 66% against and 33% for him as of July 23.
 Fox News' poll says Trump stands at 61% against and 39% for as of July 17-20.
 Reuters/Ipsos' poll says Trump stands at 63% disapproval, 33% approval as of Aug. 28-31.
 Civiqs' national polling says Trump stands at 59% against and 36% for with 6% undecided as of Aug. 31. [...] A Reuters/Ipsos poll released Aug. 31 found that 33% of Americans approved of Trump’s job performance, marking the third consecutive week at that level.

The 33% rating was Trump’s lowest in Reuters/Ipsos polling since he returned to the White House in 2025.
results.title: Trump approval rating slips among Alabama voters, new poll finds

results.content:
A new survey released Thursday shows more Missourians disapprove of President Donald Trump and Gov. Mike Kehoe’s job performance than approve.

For Trump, it is the first negative approval rating in the six-year history of the St. Louis University/YouGov poll. For Kehoe, it is the first since he took office last year.

Trump has lost 19 percentage points in net approval since he took office at the start of 2025 — including 14 points since February.
results.title: Trump, Kehoe post first negative approval ratings in new Missouri poll
